pattern-selector.why: the forces are: one fact (a checker's scope) must have one owner, and the enforcer must read it without a second copy. The fit is a self-declaring marker in the script plus one manifest section, deliberately no new abstraction and no SKILL.md frontmatter block. Rejected: a gates: block in each SKILL.md (issue 203's proposal), which would be a second copy of the scope that drifts from the marker.
pattern-selector.what: chose the marker-in-script option and recorded it with its rejected alternative in ADR-0109; the gate reads the marker as the one owner of scope.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: classifying every checker and adding a manifest section is an architecturally significant decision a future maintainer will question (why markers, why a separate consumerRequiredGates section, why not SKILL.md frontmatter).
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0109 (context, options, decision, consequences, confirmation, and the stated limits); check_adr.sh passes on it.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the classification behavior is enumerated by case for the contributor and operator audiences: a classified set passes, an unclassified checker is caught, a consumer-gate must be manifested, an upstream-only must not be listed, and a consumer-gate needs an acceptance contract.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added a feature with six tagged scenarios driven by the real gate in throwaway fixtures; bdd-run and check-bdd-executed pass.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the gate's new rules only hold if they detect a real mismark, so the tests run the real gate against throwaway skill trees and against this repo itself, not a unit test of the regex alone.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added ADR-0109 cases to the integrity test (unclassified checker, unmanifested consumer-gate, upstream-only listed, missing acceptance, sha drift, F2 testSha256, F3 nested, F4 dup-id) plus a real-repo assertion, a consumerRequiredGates case to the schema test, and a REAL-config case for the new-gate-needs-manifest routing rule.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the completeness rule is a gate, so its test must fail when the rule is neutralized: planting an unmarked check-*.mjs, an unmanifested consumer-gate, or a listed upstream-only each turns the gate red.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: each new rule has a discriminating case that fails exit 1, plus the clean real-repo case that passes exit 0; the gate fails closed on a missing/malformed manifest.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the issue's claims were taken as claims to prove, not assume: the completeness hole, the unmarked-source skip, and the never-run-in-CI gap were each verified against the code before the fix, and the fix's own claims carry re-runnable sources in ADR-0109.
skeptical-audit.what: verified gap 1 against check-upstream-manifest-integrity.mjs line 175 and the manifest, and recorded the evidence with named limits (gap 2 unclosed, provenance of the new section deferred).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the change edits a gate that governs the manifest, so it got a fresh-context review over every changed file against the four questions.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context review of the scoped diff; findings resolved or recorded, and the review entry appended to docs/arch-reviews/entries/.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the simplest thing that meets the requirement is one marker per script plus one manifest section read by the existing gate, not a new service, registry, or file format.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept the change to a self-declaring comment marker, a consumerRequiredGates array, an extension of the one gate that already reads the manifest, and one additive routing rule (no second routing config); one fact, one owner.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no untrusted input, auth, secret, or network surface: the gate reads this repo's own files and matches an anchored, bounded marker regex (no catastrophic backtracking), spawns nothing, and builds no shell string from file content.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature flag, or service rollout; the change reaches a clone through the repo and is enforced in CI.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert; a build-time classification gate covered by tests.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, no retention, migration, or backup surface; the change classifies checker scripts and extends a manifest.

arch-encode.why: the caught mistake (an unclassified consumer-facing checker) is encoded as a first-class gate rule in check-upstream-manifest-integrity.mjs with its own discrimination test, not as an arch-gate.config grep rule, so arch-encode's specific mechanism does not apply.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; Node CLIs and JSON.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the gate's violation messages name the file, the scope it is missing, and the fix in plain words for a contributor.
